## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This should not merge yet. The containment check in `preview` compares paths as text without resolving them, so a relative path containing `..` gets past it and can read files outside the home directory.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — `candidate.is_relative_to(Path(home))` only compares path components as text and never resolves `..` or symlinks. For example, `preview("/srv/home", "../../etc/passwd")` builds `/srv/home/../../etc/passwd`. That path still starts with the `/srv/home` components, so the check passes and line 14 reads `/etc/passwd`. A symlink inside home that points elsewhere gets through the same way. The added test at tests/test_paths.py:20 only tries an absolute outside path, so it misses this case. Could you resolve both sides first, e.g. `root = Path(home).resolve(); candidate = (root / relative).resolve(); if not candidate.is_relative_to(root): raise ValueError(...)`? Please also add a test for `"../outside.txt"`. — Any caller that passes a user-supplied relative path can read any file the process can access, which defeats the "outside home" protection this helper exists to provide.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- app/paths.py:14 — correctness — `candidate.read_text()[:200]` reads and decodes the whole file before keeping 200 characters. Previewing a multi-gigabyte log in the home directory loads all of it into memory. Could you open the file and call `f.read(200)` instead? — Previews of large files are slow and use a lot of memory, and a single large file can exhaust memory in the process serving previews.

## Strengths
- The two passing branches of `preview` are tested: a short file is returned unchanged and a 500-character file is cut to 200 (tests/test_paths.py:15-18).
- `settings_file` is a simple path join, and tests/test_paths.py:26 checks its exact result.
